questions.question: Certain fielding restrictions in cricket during few overs are known as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power Play**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Power Play** refers to a set of fielding restrictions in cricket during certain overs of a match.
 
• In **One Day Internationals (ODIs)**, the first 10 overs of an innings are usually designated as power play overs, where only two fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
 
• In **T20 cricket**, the power play usually lasts for the first 6 overs, with similar fielding restrictions as in ODIs.
 
• The concept of power play is designed to create a balance between bat and ball, encouraging aggressive batting while giving bowlers a chance to take wickets with fewer fielders on the boundary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fielding Restrictions:**

 
 
• Fielding restrictions in cricket are rules that limit the placement of fielders in specific areas of the field during certain periods of the game.
 
• These restrictions are aimed at ensuring a balance between the batting and bowling teams, preventing defensive field placements throughout the innings.
 
• During the power play, the fielding team is restricted to having only a limited number of fielders outside the 30-yard circle.
 
 
 
• **30-Yard Circle:**
 
 
• The 30-yard circle is a fielding restriction area in cricket, marked by a circle with a 30-yard radius from each end of the pitch.
 
• It is used to enforce fielding restrictions, particularly during power plays, ensuring that only a certain number of fielders can be placed outside this area.
 
 
 
• **One Day Internationals (ODIs):**
 
 
• ODIs are a format of limited-overs cricket, where each team faces a fixed number of overs, usually 50.
 
• Power plays are an integral part of ODIs, with fielding restrictions varying at different stages of the innings.
 
 
 
• **T20 Cricket:**
 
 
• T20 cricket is a shorter format of the game, with each team playing a single innings of 20 overs.
 
• Power plays are more aggressive in T20s, lasting for the first 6 overs, encouraging explosive batting from the outset.
